Subject: Production errors after your v3 rollout - urgent

Rachel,

We started seeing elevated 5xx and 429s across checkout predictions shortly after the update your team pushed last night (quantized model v3). Error rate peaked ~3.8% between 13:00-14:20 PT and many of our retry loops caused request queuing on our side. This affected payment validation flows for ~20% of requests and caused timeouts in our user checkout path.

Attached are a few sample request IDs and a short stack trace from our service. Can your team confirm if this rollout included kernel changes or a different quantization profile? We need an ETA for mitigation—this is impacting a major campaign tonight.

- Miguel
Director, Platform Engineering
MerchantX

FYI everybody — I've pulled the first pass of telemetry. High-level:
- 5xx rate rose from 0.12% baseline to ~3.6% across the v3 pool.
- 429s concentrated on the small shard of low-memory hosts (edge autoscale event triggered retries).
- Latency p50 shifted +30ms; p95 increased by ~420ms during the spike.

I'm attaching a trace bundle and a config diff between v2 and v3 (model-config-diff.txt). Early sign: per-channel int8 paths are hitting a fallback code-path on older kernels which results in a repeated KV cache miss and a per-token retry attempt in the runtime. That aligns with MerchantX's retry storms.

Immediate ask: Markus, can you trigger a partial rollback to v2 on the MerchantX routing policy while we confirm the kernel compatibility? If rollback isn't safe right away, we should throttle or route MerchantX to the v2 model variant.

Markus/Rachel —

We see kernel-level warnings for AVX-compatibility on a subset of nodes (older driver stack). The per-channel int8 code path triggers a software fallback that does extra validation and a KV cache invalidation on first token, which can cascade with aggressive client retries. Recommendation:
1) Pause per-channel int8 rollout on fleets running old drivers.
2) Apply driver patch (v460.42) to the affected shards — ETA 3 hours for non-disruptive patching.
3) In parallel, continue routing MerchantX to v2 and widen rollback if errors persist.

We'll prioritize the affected hosts and provide status updates.

— Cloud Partner Support

Draft summary below for Rachel to send to leadership and MerchantX CTO: 

Subject: Incident report — MerchantX elevated 5xx/429 after quantized v3 rollout

Summary: Between 13:00-14:20 PT on 2026-11-09, MerchantX observed elevated 5xx and 429 rates affecting checkout traffic. Peak 5xx ~3.8% (baseline 0.12%). Root cause (current hypothesis): per-channel int8 quantization on model v3 triggers a fallback code-path on older kernel/driver stacks, causing KV cache invalidations and repeated runtime retries. This combined with MerchantX client retries produced a retry storm and increased tail latency.

Containment: Partial rollback initiated at 15:47 PT (40% traffic to v2). MerchantX routing pinned to v2-compatible binary. Edge autoscale adjusted to reduce low-memory shard pressure.

Next steps: 1) Continue rollback until 95% stability achieved or driver patch applied. 2) Cloud partner to patch drivers (ETA ~3h). 3) Post-mortem to include kernel compatibility test in our release gating + new routing fallback to prefer non-quantized variant when client retry rates exceed threshold.

ETA / owner: Full containment expected within 3 hours (Markus), cloud patch owner: Cloud Partner, communications owner: Rachel.

—Stephanie

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@merchantx.com>

Subject: Incident update & exec note for MerchantX CTO

Miguel —

Thanks again for the rapid report and for sharing request IDs. Quick executive note below that I shared with our leadership and your CTO:

— Incident summary (executive): MerchantX experienced elevated 5xx/429 rates after a quantized model v3 rollout that exercised a per-channel int8 codepath. On older host drivers this triggered a runtime fallback causing KV cache invalidations and repeated token-level retries. Combined with client retries, we observed a retry-storm that impacted checkout latency and caused timeouts for ~20% of requests during the peak window.

— Actions taken: Partial rollback to v2 (40% traffic) completed; routing pinned to v2-compatible binary for MerchantX; cloud partner identified driver incompatibility and is patching affected hosts (ETA ~3 hours).

— Next steps & ETA: Expect full containment once drivers are patched or rollback widened to 95% of traffic. SRE will monitor RPS, 5xx/429, and tail latency in 15-minute intervals and share updates. Post-mortem will propose release gating for quantization + kernel matrix compatibility checks.

We will continue to prioritize this. I will send another update once the patch is applied or if we see the rollback effectuate full containment.

—Rachel
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
